title: Return from an anchor state
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and choose find and startup modes. For an input word $x$, configuration $c$ of $B$ on $x$, release bit $r$, time $t$, word $w$, and configuration $f$ of $F$ on $x$, suppose the run of $B$ from $c$ is in state $a$ at time $t$, that $r$ is false if $t=0$, and that at every earlier time $u<t$ either $u=0$ and $r$ is true or the run is not in state $a$. Then after $t+1$ steps the host machine, started with the corresponding body-call configuration, is exactly in the call configuration formed from the time-$t$ body configuration with its state set to halted, release set to false, and flag set to false; the word, fuel configuration, and other supplied data are preserved.
hypotheses_covered: The body run is in state $a$ at time $t$
